statement: For every Δ>log 2, let q=2e^(−Δ)/(1+2e^(−Δ)), let κ_j be the j-th derivative at zero of log(1−q+q cosh z), and let m_*(Δ)=min{m≥2: (−1)^(m+1)κ_(2m)(q)<0}. This minimum exists. If a=arcosh(e^Δ/2), β=arctan(a/π), and t=π/(4β), then for all sufficiently small a>0 one has t<m_*(Δ)≤ceil(t+1)<t+2. Consequently a m_*(Δ)→π²/4 as Δ↓log 2, equivalently lim_(ε↓0) sqrt(ε)m_*(log 2+ε)=π²/(4sqrt(2)).
contribution: A complete proof of the frozen critical first-failure asymptotic, based on an exact absolutely convergent zero-sum formula that controls every preceding integer order. It also gives the stronger two-lattice-step localization of m_* near π/[4 arctan(a/π)]. The cited 2026 source proves only fixed-parameter eventual failure; a bounded current search found no equivalent uniform first-failure result, but no priority claim is made.
